title: Nscale’s AI Buildout Hit by Fire, Delays and Angry Workers Ahead of IPO
key_facts: Bloomberg reported on 15 Oct 2026 that Nscale's flagship Narvik, Norway data center, built with Aker, has had cooling leaks, permitting fights, construction delays and a fire
Only 6.4 of a planned 30 megawatts is running; Startup Fortune says the site is six months behind schedule
Workers are housed on a floating hotel to keep the build moving
Nscale filed to list on the NYSE under NSCL at a valuation of roughly $35 billion
Revenue for six months to 30 June was $140.6 million; net loss $1.02 billion
Microsoft and Anthropic are anchor customers with multi-year deals worth close to $88 billion together, per the article
Nscale says about 289,000 GPUs are active and contracted versus roughly 25,000 running today
quote_evidence: Bloomberg reported on October 15 that Nscale's flagship Norway data center is six months behind schedule, with only 6.4 of its planned 30 megawatts actually running.
Nscale's revenue for the six months ended June 30 came in at $140.6 million, up sharply from $10.4 million a year earlier.
Net losses over the same period jumped to $1.02 billion, from $369 million the year before.
why_it_matters_hint: The gap between contracted and running AI capacity is the core risk for an IPO investor.
notes: Bloomberg page blocked (403); read Startup Fortune, which summarizes it. Startup Fortune adds its own commentary (CoreWeave comparison), not used here.
